name: Tawang Monastery (Gaden Namgyal Lhatse)
description: Largest Buddhist monastery in India and one of the largest in the world, belonging to the Gelugpa sect. Founded in 1680-81 by Merak Lama Lodre Gyatso under the guidance of the 5th Dalai Lama; houses a large Buddha statue, ancient scriptures and offers panoramic views of the Tawang Chu valley.
facts: Founded 1680-81 by Merak Lama Lodre Gyatso
Birthplace connection to 6th Dalai Lama nearby

name: Sangetsar Tso (Madhuri Lake)
description: High-altitude lake on the route toward Bum La Pass, formed by an earthquake that submerged a forest, leaving dead tree trunks standing in the water. Popularly known as Madhuri Lake after a Bollywood film shoot; surrounded by rugged Himalayan peaks.
facts: Army permit often required for access

name: Sela Pass
description: High-altitude mountain pass at about 4,170 m on the border of Tawang and West Kameng districts, carrying NH-13 and the primary road link to Tawang. Often snow-covered; features Sela Lake nearby and dramatic Himalayan views. Recently improved with Sela Tunnel.
facts: On border of Tawang and West Kameng
Connects Tawang to Dirang and Assam
Named linked to 1962 war local legend

name: Nuranang Falls (Jang Falls)
description: Approximately 100 m high curtain waterfall near Jang town on the Tawang-Bomdila road. Fed by the Nuranang Chu originating from Sela Pass slopes; popular roadside stop with hydel plant nearby and featured in Bollywood songs.
facts: Also called Jang or Bong Bong Falls
About 40 km from Tawang near Jang
Song from film Koyla shot here

name: Urgelling Monastery
description: Historic Buddhist monastery and birthplace of the 6th Dalai Lama Tsangyang Gyatso (born 1683). Founded around 1489 by Urgen Sangpo; smaller and quieter than Tawang Monastery, located a few kilometres from Tawang town.

name: Tawang War Memorial
description: Memorial in the form of a Buddhist stupa/chorten dedicated to Indian soldiers who lost their lives in the 1962 Sino-Indian War. Located on a hill overlooking Tawang town; names of fallen inscribed on granite, surrounded by prayer flags.

name: Gorsam Chorten
description: Large Buddhist stupa near Zemithang, about 90 km from Tawang, modelled on Boudhanath in Nepal. Believed built in 12th-18th century by Monpa lama; features circumambulation path and is a major local pilgrimage site, especially during Gorsam Kora.
facts: Largest chorten in the Tawang area

name: Tawang Town
description: District headquarters and main tourist base in Tawang district at about 3,000 m elevation. Gateway for exploring the monastery, lakes, passes and Monpa culture; connected by NH-13 via Sela Pass.
facts: Base for Tawang Monastery and nearby sites

name: Zemithang
description: Remote border village in western Tawang district near the Bhutan and Tibet trijunction, about 85-90 km from Tawang. Base for Gorsam Chorten and scenic valley; historically significant during 1962 war.
facts: About 85-90 km west of Tawang via Lumla

name: Pangateng Tso (PT Tso / Pankang Teng Tso)
description: High-altitude lake about 16-18 km north of Tawang on the road toward Bum La. Often frozen in winter; surrounded by mountains and rhododendrons, popular for scenic drives and picnics.
